conclusion: Every backtest vote (2023, 2024 and the optional 2025 vote) predates all three pre-training cutoffs, so a good backtest score could partly reflect memorised results. A leakage probe (ask the bare model the result, directly and disguised) must be run and shown next to the backtest.

paris_streets_2025.direct: What was the official result of the Paris 'votation' held on 23 March 2025 on greening and pedestrianising 500 more streets? What share of valid votes was 'Pour', and what was the turnout?
paris_streets_2025.disguised: Imagine Paris asks registered voters (aged 16+), in a Sunday vote with no other election, 'Pour ou contre végétaliser et rendre piétonnes 500 nouvelles rues dans Paris, réparties dans tous les quartiers ?'. Estimate the 'Pour' share among valid votes and the turnout.

outOfSampleCandidates.what: Paris municipal elections, 15 and 22 March 2026 (results by arrondissement on paris.fr)
outOfSampleFor: Nemotron 3 Ultra pre-training only (its post-training data runs to May 2026)
outOfSampleCandidates.comparability: Low-medium: a candidate election, not a yes/no measure. It can test the sim's political geography (e.g. does simulated support for 'green streets' measures track the left-list vote by sector?).
outOfSampleCandidates.reported: Emmanuel Grégoire (left union) elected mayor; reported 50.52 % in the second round (press; not checked against official files).

sources.name: paris.fr — Élections municipales 2026: tous les résultats en cartes
Public Sénat — Emmanuel Grégoire élu maire de Paris

outOfSampleCandidates.what: Le Bourget data-centre controversy (petition, public inquiry, permit withdrawn)
outOfSampleFor: Nemotron 3 Nano and Super pre-training (both end June 2025)
outOfSampleCandidates.comparability: Qualitative only (no vote): checks whether simulated objections to the hypothetical data centre match the arguments real residents raised after the cutoff — fire/battery risk, generators and air pollution, noise, heat island, grid use, PFAS refrigerant, few jobs.
